# Live handoff — deep-research review of the Full Corpus

**Generated by `scripts/research-handoff.mjs` on every `npm run validate`. Do not edit.**

This file is the answer to "what is current?" — check it rather than asking. It is rewritten
from committed state on every validate run, so if it says something, that is what the corpus
says right now.

It carries no commit SHA and no branch name on purpose. Either would make this file change
on commits that touch nothing you care about, and neither is what you need — the unit
fingerprints are, and those move only when the candidate they cover moves.

| | |
|---|---|
| Executable set | 34 families |
| Review units | 126 — 55 × A (source descriptions), 69 × B (whole-document), 2 × C (re-source) |

Machine-readable equivalent: [`research-state.json`](research-state.json).

## Read these first

1. [`DEEP_RESEARCH_BRIEF.md`](DEEP_RESEARCH_BRIEF.md) — what six completed passes already
   settled, so you do not re-ask those questions, and what the three remaining ones look for.
2. [`research-tasks/README.md`](research-tasks/README.md) — the task index. One file per
   family; work order C → B → A.
3. [`README.md`](README.md) — the review index, if you want the whole history.

## Your verdict does not go stale just because the corpus moved

Every reviewable unit carries a **fingerprint** over the only material a verdict is about:
the candidate's text, its basis, and its provenance. Put that fingerprint in your verdict.

The record's own content hash covers the whole record, so repairing a citation in `pub1`
moves it — and would invalidate a finding about `exp2` for no reason. The gate therefore
checks **your unit**, not the record. A verdict is refused only when the thing you actually
read has changed, and the refusal names it.

So: work at your own pace, return verdicts as you finish them, and re-run the gate whenever
you like. If something you reviewed has been repaired since, it will tell you which unit and
you re-read that one. Nothing else you have returned is affected.

```
node scripts/ingest-research-verdicts.mjs
```

## What this review is and is not

It is not the release gate and it sets nothing on any record. The corpus stays a
release-candidate with `reviewed_by_human` false on all records until a human decides
otherwise. What this makes possible is assessing that decision from repository state rather
than from someone's memory of who looked at what.
